expectations.text: Identifies SQL injection in GET /orders where req.query.userId is concatenated into the query string (CWE-89)

expectations.text: Identifies broken access control / IDOR in GET /orders/:id — the order is fetched by id with no check that it belongs to req.user (CWE-639)
expectations.evidence: High finding: 'IDOR: any order readable by ID, with full-row exposure (CWE-639 + CWE-200) — orders.js:18-21, GET /orders/:id' — 'no user_id predicate and no post-fetch ownership comparison'.

expectations.text: Identifies mass assignment in PATCH /orders/:id — req.body is passed straight into Order.update, letting the client set fields like status/total/user_id (CWE-915)
expectations.evidence: Critical finding: 'Mass assignment — raw req.body into Order.update (CWE-915) — orders.js:28' — cites {"total":0,"status":"paid","user_id":<attacker_id>} exactly.

expectations.text: Identifies the unvalidated refund amount in POST /orders/:id/refund — no sign/upper-bound check allows negative or over-refund (business-logic / CWE-839)
expectations.evidence: Critical finding: 'Unvalidated refund amount — negative and over-refund (CWE-840 / CWE-839) — orders.js:34, 37' — '{"amount": -100}' and '{"amount": 999999}' over-refunds a $10 order; no sign check, no upper bound.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT report the parameterized queries using `$1` placeholders (in GET/PATCH /orders/:id) as SQL injection
expectations.evidence: 'Considered and cleared': 'GET /orders/:id and the PATCH pre-flight query (lines 19, 26) — use $1 bound parameters correctly; not SQL injection. Only the GET /orders query is injectable.' No SQLi is attributed to the $1 queries anywhere.

expectations.text: Flags SHA-256 used for password storage in hash_password — no key stretching, needs bcrypt/argon2id (CWE-916)
expectations.evidence: Finding #4 'Passwords hashed with unsalted single-round SHA-256' (lines 18-19, consumed at line 25), CWE-916; fix recommends Argon2id/bcrypt.

expectations.text: Flags jwt.decode called without an algorithms allowlist in current_user — enables algorithm-confusion / 'none' acceptance (CWE-327/CWE-347)
expectations.evidence: Finding #1 'JWT verified without an algorithm allowlist', line 32 jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET), CWE-347/CWE-327; explicitly covers alg:none and algorithm-confusion.

expectations.text: Flags the password-reset token generated with uuid.uuid1() as predictable (time/MAC-based, not cryptographically random) (CWE-330)
expectations.evidence: Finding #2 'Password-reset token is a predictable UUIDv1', line 41, CWE-330; explains timestamp + host MAC node ID, not a CSPRNG.

expectations.text: Flags verify=False disabling TLS certificate verification on the requests.post billing call (CWE-295)
expectations.evidence: Finding #6 'TLS certificate verification disabled on the internal billing call', line 48 requests.post(..., verify=False), CWE-295.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT flag hmac.compare_digest in verify_webhook as a timing-unsafe comparison (it is the correct constant-time function)
expectations.evidence: Considered-and-cleared: 'the signature comparison itself *is* constant-time'. #11 flags login()'s != as non-constant-time (different, legitimate); #13 is only the non-ASCII TypeError edge. compare_digest itself never called timing-unsafe.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT flag secrets.token_urlsafe in new_api_key as weak/predictable randomness (it is a correct CSPRNG)
expectations.evidence: Considered-and-cleared: 'new_api_key() (line 57) — secrets.token_urlsafe(32) is a CSPRNG with 256 bits of entropy. Correct.'

expectations.evidence: Finding 1 'Unauthenticated full-read SSRF in the image proxy' (critical, CWE-918): req.query.url → await fetch(url) with 'no scheme check, no host allowlist, no post-DNS IP validation, and no redirect restriction'. Fix names 10/8, 169.254/16, etc. deny-list.

expectations.text: Flags the user-configurable webhook targetUrl in POST /webhooks stored with no allowlist / SSRF validation (CWE-918)
expectations.evidence: Finding 4 'Stored SSRF via unvalidated webhook targetUrl' (high, CWE-918): 'Any authenticated user persists an arbitrary destination URL ... with no scheme check, no internal-range block' at lines 20-23.

expectations.text: Notes that /proxy/image pipes the upstream response body back to the caller, turning the SSRF into a data-exfiltration / internal-response-disclosure channel
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: 'the response body is piped back verbatim' and 'Because the body is returned rather than discarded, this is *read* SSRF, not blind: no oracle-building required.' Exploit returns IMDS AccessKeyId/SecretAccessKey/Token in the body.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT report GET /assets/:id as SSRF — the host is a fixed internal CDN_BASE and only a validated positive integer id is user-controlled

notes: NON-DISCRIMINATING: pass rate is 100% in BOTH configurations across all 5 evals / 26 assertions. Every planted vuln was caught and all 10 safe traps cleared by both the with-skill and the baseline (own-knowledge) reviewer. On this test set the assertion score cannot tell the two apart.

COST: the skill costs 1.78x tokens (mean 96.8k vs 54.2k) and 1.78x wall-clock (mean 240s vs 135s) — the overhead of loading SKILL.md + 3-5 reference files — with no measured recall or precision gain on these files.

EVAL BLIND SPOT (flagged independently by 3 of 5 graders): assertions reward only the PLANTED items. The with-skill reviews surfaced extra LEGITIMATE findings that no assertion credits — reflected Content-Type -> same-origin XSS (proxy.js); query-string PII, model-alias pinning, missing audit logging (chat_endpoint.py); findUser over-fetch (account.js). The skill's most likely real benefit (thoroughness) is invisible to current scoring.

PRECISION CRUCIBLE DID NOT TRIGGER OVER-FLAGGING: on account.js both arms reported ~7-8 findings but ZERO were false positives on the 5 named safe traps; both explicitly 'considered and cleared' each trap with correct reasoning. Baseline precision matched with-skill.

INTERPRETATION: against a frontier base model these textbook-severity vulns are already in-weights, so the skill neither adds catches nor prevents FPs here; the 100% ceiling means the test set is too easy to discriminate. To measure the skill's value, iteration 2 needs (a) subtler/rarer vulns where base knowledge is thin, (b) metrics for TOTAL true-positives and TOTAL false-positives rather than planted-item recall, and optionally (c) a weaker/cheaper executor model where skill guidance has more headroom.
